question: is there a weight at which delivery becomes risky?

sources.title: Cochrane Library — Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
Influence of maternal body mass index on pregnancy complications and outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis - PMC

text: Your doctor makes the medical call. There isn’t one single weight where delivery suddenly becomes risky. Suspected large baby weight is linked with shoulder dystocia, birth injury, longer labour, assisted delivery and postpartum haemorrhage, but weight estimates are imprecise and can be off by about 8%–15% [1][2][3]. Higher maternal BMI is also linked with more caesarean birth, induction, hypertensive disorders and postpartum haemorrhage [4].
